---
title: The Graph Widget
order: 20
---

The graph widget can be added to any page in two forms:

- **Full graph view**: place the `{{{< quarto-graph-full >}}}` shortcode
  on any page you choose, this page for an example: [[Graph]].  This view shows every page by default. Drag nodes, scroll to zoom, click
  a node to open that page. Multiple instances on one page are fine, each
  with its own params. See [Customizing the full graph widget](#customizing-the-full-graph-widget).
- **Sidebar mini-panel**: on every page, a small N-depth subgraph (the
  current page plus everything within N links of it; 1-depth by default)
  mounts at the top of the right-hand TOC sidebar. Clicking it opens a
  larger modal version of the same subgraph. Shows alongside the full
  graph view too, if a page has both.

## What graph.json looks like

`graph.json` contains an array of nodes and edges. Here's a minimal example
with two nodes (Backlinks and The Graph Widget) and one edge between them:

```json
{
  "nodes": [
    {"rel": "concepts/backlinks/index.qmd", "title": "Backlinks", "bucket": "concepts", "depth": 2, "colors": {"by-folder": "#e69f00", "by-depth": "#440154"}, "url": "/backlinks/"},
    {"rel": "concepts/the-graph-widget/index.qmd", "title": "The Graph Widget", "bucket": "concepts", "depth": 2, "colors": {"by-folder": "#e69f00", "by-depth": "#3b518b"}, "url": "/the-graph-widget/"}
  ],
  "edges": [[0, 1]],
  "schemes": {
    "by-folder": {"by": "folder", "palette": "okabe-ito", "legend": [{"bucket": "concepts", "color": "#e69f00"}]},
    "by-depth": {"by": "depth", "palette": "viridis", "legend": [{"bucket": 2, "color": "#440154"}]}
  },
  "default-scheme": "by-folder"
}
```

Edges are pairs of node indices; `[0, 1]` connects the first and second
nodes. Each node carries a `bucket` (its top-level folder, or `(root)` for
the project's own top-level pages), a path `depth`, and a `colors` map with
one hex per color scheme, so a widget can switch schemes without graph.js
knowing any palette. `schemes` also carries each scheme's `legend` (bucket
to color), which the full graph widget renders.

`graph.json` is assembled in two passes: pre-render builds the registry
and backlink map from every page's wikilinks and writes it to a
side-channel file; then, at each page's own render time, its Lua filter
records that page's real output URL to another side-channel file. Post-render
joins the two and writes the final `graph.json` into the output
directory. This late join is why a wikilink resolves to a real URL only
after the whole project has rendered, not up front.

## Node colors

Node colors come from **color schemes**, defined in `_quarto.yml` under
`quarto-graph: color:`. A scheme says how to bucket a page (`by`) and which
palette to assign to those buckets (`palette`). By default pages are
colored **by folder** using the colorblind-safe **Okabe-Ito** palette,
which emphasizes the structural split between topics. Two built-in schemes
exist, and you can override them or add your own:

```yaml
quarto-graph:
  color:
    default-scheme: by-folder   # which scheme widgets use by default
    schemes:
      by-folder: {by: folder, palette: okabe-ito}   # the default
      by-depth:  {by: depth, palette: viridis}      # nesting depth shades
```

| Key | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `by-folder` (built-in default) | bucket = top-level folder (`(root)` for top-level pages); qualitative palette |
| `by-depth` (built-in) | bucket = path depth (0 at root, 1 = `a/index.qmd`, ...); sequential palette |
| `custom` | exact `custom: {bucket: hex}` map; any bucket not listed falls back to gray |

`palette` values: `okabe-ito` (7 colorblind-safe colors, the default),
`d3-category10` (10 categorical colors), or `viridis` (sequential — pairs
naturally with `by: depth`). When a qualitative palette has more folders
than it has colors, extra buckets get auto-generated maximally-spread
colors, so a project with any number of folders still gets distinct hues.

For a custom scheme (project-wide; `custom:` keys are folder names):

```yaml
quarto-graph:
  color:
    default-scheme: my-pal
    schemes:
      my-pal:
        by: custom
        custom:
          concepts: "#ee7733"
          reference: "#0077bb"
```

## Customizing the full graph widget

`{{{< quarto-graph-full >}}}` takes kwargs, all optional:

| Kwarg | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `width` | Any CSS length (`"600px"`, `"80%"`, `"50vw"`) applied to the widget's container. Default: fills its container. |
| `height` | Any CSS length. Default: `max(420px, 65% of viewport height)`. |
| `depth` | Show only pages within N links of `root` (or the current page, if `root` is omitted), instead of the whole project graph. |
| `root` | The page to center `depth` on. Matched the same way a `[[wikilink]]` is: by title, alias, or filename stem first, falling back to a literal source path (e.g. `posts/foo.qmd`) if nothing matches. Ignored unless `depth` is also set. |
| `expandable` | `"true"` adds a button that expands the widget to a fullscreen overlay. Default: off. |
| `color-scheme` | Color this widget with a scheme name from `quarto-graph: color: schemes:` (`"by-folder"`, `"by-depth"`, or your own), overriding the project default for this widget only. Unknown names fall back to the default scheme's colors. |

Multiple widgets, each with its own color scheme, on one page is
supported — the widget's per-widget `color-scheme` overrides only that
instance:

```markdown
{{{< quarto-graph-full >}}}

{{{< quarto-graph-full color-scheme="by-depth" height="50vh" >}}}

{{{< quarto-graph-full color-scheme="my-pal" width="60%" expandable="true" >}}}
```

Each `{{{< quarto-graph-full >}}}` call is independent. Color does have a
project-wide default (`color: default-scheme:`), but each widget's own
`color-scheme` kwarg overrides it for that instance only, as shown above.
A `root` that doesn't match any page logs a warning at render time and that
particular widget renders nothing, rather than silently falling back to the
whole graph.

## Configuring the sidebar mini-panel

The full graph view is always opt-in, placed by the `{{{< quarto-graph-full >}}}`
shortcode. The sidebar mini-panel opt-out by default,  meaning unless explicitly configured off, every page will show a 1-depth graph of the current page.

Global default, in `_quarto.yml`:

```yaml
quarto-graph:
  sidebar: true   # shorthand for {enabled: true, depth: 1}, both defaults
```

Or spell out either field:

```yaml
quarto-graph:
  sidebar:
    enabled: true
    depth: 2
```

Per-page override, same key, in that page's own frontmatter, either the
bare bool or the `{enabled, depth}` form:

```yaml
---
title: My Page
quarto-graph:
  sidebar:
    depth: 3   # this page only; enabled still inherits the project default
---
```

A page's override only replaces the field(s) it actually sets: overriding
just `depth:` keeps the project's `enabled`, and vice versa.

| `_quarto.yml` `sidebar` | page `sidebar` | mini-panel shows? |
|---|---|---|
| `true` (default) | unset | yes, depth 1 |
| `true` | `false` | no |
| `false` | unset | no |
| `false` | `true` | yes, depth 1 |
| `{enabled: true, depth: 2}` | `{depth: 3}` | yes, depth 3 |

If the page has no sidebar, meaning TOC is set tofalse, or using a custom layout, the sidebar minipanel will not display.
